plan.title: bug(run-summary): seq is 1 on every emitted line - per-process emitter never seeds from the target file; seqSeed has no callers (#3320 post-close residual)

narratives.Description: Every collected field run-summary JSONL line currently carries seq: 1 because each CLI process constructs a fresh emitter. The schema documents a monotonic per-emitter sequence, but seqSeed has no callers, so consumers cannot rely on seq for order.
narratives.UserStory: As a telemetry consumer, I want run-summary seq to be monotonic across CLI invocations that append to the same file, so that I can order events without silently falling back to ts.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: Implement Option A in packages/core/src/run-summary/emit.ts: when the destination is a file, seed seq from the current line count of the append-only JSONL at emitter construction. Keep stdout destination per-process. Add a test that covers multiple constructor/CLI invocations into one file. Update the schema comment and CHANGELOG #3350.
narratives.Overview:
**TL;DR: every line in collected field run-summary JSONL carries `seq: 1`. The schema documents "monotonic per-emitter sequence (1-based)", but every real event comes from a separate CLI process, each constructing a fresh emitter. The `seqSeed` reuse mechanism exists in `packages/core/src/run-summary/emit.ts` but has no callers. A field that promises ordering and never delivers will get built against; ordering currently falls back silently to `ts`.**

(Originally reported as a comment on #3320 after it closed — re-filed so it has an open home.)

**Evidence:** collected field telemetry (internal benchmark, private) shows `seq: 1` on 100% of lines across all trials on both releases that have shipped the emitter. At HEAD: `emitRunSummaryEvent` ("one-shot helper for call sites that do not hold an emitter") constructs `new RunSummaryEmitter(...)` per call; grep for `seqSeed` finds only its own doc comment.

## Fix (pick one, thin)

- **Option A (preferred):** when the destination is a file, seed `seq` from the current line count of the target file at emitter construction (the file is append-only JSONL; count-then-append gives a monotonic per-session sequence with no extra state). Stdout destination keeps per-process seq and the docs say so.
- **Option B:** drop the field and document `ts` as the order key.

Either way the schema comment stops promising something the wire never delivers.

## Acceptance sketch

- A session producing N events into one `DEFT_RUN_SUMMARY_PATH` file yields seq 1..N (option A), or the field is gone and docs name `ts` (option B).
- Test covers the multiple-CLI-invocation case, not just one emitter instance.

Relates #3320 (shipped the denominator; this defect was reported there post-close), #3282 (emitter).

items.title: Seed file-destination seq from existing JSONL line count (Option A)

narrative.Acceptance: Given N prior events already in DEFT_RUN_SUMMARY_PATH, when a new CLI process constructs a file-destination emitter and emits, seq continues as N+1 rather than resetting to 1. Stdout destination keeps per-process seq and docs say so.
Given a test that invokes emit across separate process/construction boundaries into one file, when it runs, it asserts seq 1..N across invocations (not just one emitter instance).
Given the schema comment that promised monotonic per-emitter seq, when this lands, the comment matches wire behavior and CHANGELOG [Unreleased] cites #3350.
